raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Summary (DeepSeek-V3 4-layer proxy, 8x MI355X, Mega MoE before -> after the Primus-Turbo change;
numbers from the Primus-Turbo PRs):

| precision | peak memory | TFLOP/s per GPU | loss | source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| MXFP8 | 162.4 -> 149.3 GB (**-13.1 GB, -8.1%**) | 1118.4 -> 1131.3 (+1.2%) | same curve | [Primus-Turbo #566](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus-Turbo/pull/566) |
| BF16 | 152.9 -> 122.3 GB (**-30.6 GB, -20.0%**) | 962.6 -> 955.5 (-0.7%) | same curve | [Primus-Turbo #568](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus-Turbo/pull/568) |

# Description

Primus-Turbo #566 (MXFP8) and #568 (BF16) stop sizing every per-layer Mega MoE tensor at the
worst-case receive pool. Each layer reads the rows dispatched to this rank back once, after its
routing prologue, and allocates to them. This PR moves Primus onto that Primus-Turbo revision.
Primus's MegaMoE integration is unchanged; the work is in the CI image the new Primus-Turbo needs.

## Changes

- **Primus-Turbo `67b8e093` -> `de8fa6ca`**: #566, #568, the FlyDSL 0.3.4.1 / AITER v0.1.24.post1
  upgrade (#544) and MI455X optimization v1 (#567). AITER moves to v0.1.24.post1 with it.
- **CI base image `rocm/primus:v26.5` -> `v26.8`**, Triton 3.7.0 -> 3.9.0 (`release/3.9.x`). AITER
  installs with `AITER_USE_SYSTEM_TRITON=1`, so the pinned Triton stays the only one.
- **`-ainic` image:** v26.8 already carries the AINIC stack, so `-ainic` is the same image under that
  tag. The `Dockerfile.ainic` build stays in the workflow, commented out: it builds rccl rocm-7.1.0,
  which needs `rocm_smi`, and the ROCm 10.1 SDK in v26.8 no longer ships it.

## Behaviour changes

- **Mega MoE syncs with the host once per layer**, in both precisions, so a layer that contains it
  can no longer be captured in a CUDA graph. `examples/megatron/models/deepseek-v4/run_deepseek_v4.sh`
  still suggests full-layer capture with MegaMoE.
- **FlyDSL 0.3.4.1:** Primus's own FlyDSL kernels still target 0.2.4 and fail to import under it: the
  Kimi-K3 `_flydsl_v1` kernels and the DeepSeek-V4 `flydsl_v1` attention backend. They need a port to
  the 0.3.x API.

## Testing

- CI image build of this branch (`tasimage/primus:pr-1271`).
- On that image, 8x MI355X: the DeepSeek-V3 4-layer proxy trains 15 iterations with bf16 and MXFP8
  Mega MoE.

nodes.body:
### 🟡 Changes recommended The FlyDSL upgrade breaks existing native kernel imports, including DeepSeek-V4 model construction when selecting `flydsl_v1`.
1 open issue - [flydsl upgrade breaks DeepSeek-V4 flydsl_v1 backend imports](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1271#discussion_r4321122571) · New
What changed in this PR Updates the CI image’s paired Primus-Turbo and AITER dependencies and removes stale AITER modules before installation. **Changes:** - Pins Primus-Turbo to `de8fa6ca` and AITER to `v0.1.24.post1`. - Deletes leftover AITER package directories after uninstalling the base version. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | `.github/​workflows/​docker/​Dockerfile` | Removes stale AITER modules before reinstalling. | | `.github/​workflows/​ci.yaml` | Updates dependency pins and explanatory comments. |
Review effort: Balanced

This pin installs `flydsl==0.3.4.1`, which removes `flydsl.expr.vector`. In addition to the Kimi-K3 kernels acknowledged in the description, DeepSeek-V4's native `flydsl_v1` forward and backward kernels still import it (`v4_attention_kernels/_flydsl_v1/dsa_fwd_v4_flydsl_kernel.py:52` and `dsa_bwd_dq_flydsl_kernel.py:52`). Selecting either `use_v4_attention_backend=flydsl_v1` or `use_v4_csa_attention_backend=flydsl_v1` on gfx950 calls `load_flydsl_attention_backends()` during layer initialization and now raises `ImportError`. This affects model construction, not just kernel tests. Port the affected Primus kernels alongside this upgrade, or retain the compatible Turbo/AITER dependency pair until the port is ready.

nodes.body:
### 🔵 Needs a closer look The new Turbo pin breaks the existing BF16 MegaMoE full-layer CUDA-graph configuration.
1 open issue - [flydsl upgrade breaks DeepSeek-V4 flydsl_v1 backend imports](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1271#discussion_r4321122571)
1 previously missed issue In code that hasn't changed since last review
Turbo MegaMoE revision breaks CUDA-graph capture `.github/​workflows/​ci.yaml:48` This Turbo revision makes BF16 MegaMoE incompatible with CUDA-graph capture: it reads the dispatched row count back to the host to size buffers. The upstream commit explicitly removes its graph-capture tests for this reason. Primus still enables full-layer capture when `USE_TURBO_MEGA_MOE=True ENABLE_CUDA_GRAPH=True` in `examples/megatron/models/deepseek-v4/run_deepseek_v4.sh`, so that configuration now fails during capture. Reject graph scopes that include the MegaMoE expert path with a clear configuration error, or exclude that path from capture before adopting this pin.
Review effort: Balanced

### 🔵 Needs a closer look The Turbo upgrade breaks the supported BF16 MegaMoE full-layer CUDA-graph configuration without compatibility handling.
1 open issue - [flydsl upgrade breaks DeepSeek-V4 flydsl_v1 backend imports](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1271#discussion_r4321122571)
1 previously missed issue In code that hasn't changed since last review
Turbo MegaMoE pin breaks BF16 full-layer CUDA graph capture `.github/​workflows/​ci.yaml:48` This Turbo pin makes BF16 MegaMoE incompatible with full-layer CUDA graphs: each forward now reads the dispatched row count back to the host, and the pinned op explicitly documents that it is not capturable. `MegaMoEExperts.forward` calls the affected `fused_mega_moe_stage1` directly, while `examples/megatron/models/deepseek-v4/run_deepseek_v4.sh:116-126` still recommends full-layer capture with MegaMoE. Enabling `ENABLE_CUDA_GRAPH=True USE_TURBO_MEGA_MOE=True` with the default BF16 expert precision will therefore fail during capture. Add compatibility handling that excludes MegaMoE from capture or rejects this combination with an actionable error, and update the launcher guidance alongside the pin.
Review effort: Balanced

### 🔵 Needs a closer look The upgraded MegaMoE cannot support the full-layer CUDA-graph configuration still recommended by the launcher.
1 open issue - [flydsl upgrade breaks DeepSeek-V4 flydsl_v1 backend imports](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1271#discussion_r4321122571)
1 previously missed issue In code that hasn't changed since last review
MegaMoE CUDA graph capture fails with host synchronization `.github/​workflows/​ci.yaml:48` This pin adopts Turbo #568's host-synchronizing BF16 MegaMoE forward, which cannot be captured in a CUDA graph. However, `examples/megatron/models/deepseek-v4/run_deepseek_v4.sh:116–126` still recommends MegaMoE with full-layer capture and selects that scope when `USE_TURBO_MEGA_MOE=True ENABLE_CUDA_GRAPH=True` is set without a scope override. That previously supported launch now fails during capture. Reject capture scopes that include MegaMoE before capture starts, or select a verified scope that excludes it, and remove the recipe's sync-free capture recommendation.
Review effort: Balanced

### 🟡 Changes recommended The dependency upgrade breaks existing FlyDSL backends and leaves incompatible MegaMoE graph capture selectable.
3 open issues - [Prevent CUDA graph capture from including MegaMoE](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1271#discussion_r4331754172) · New - [Port MiniMax and DeepSeek kernels to new FlyDSL API](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1271#discussion_r4331754235) · New - [flydsl upgrade breaks DeepSeek-V4 flydsl_v1 backend imports](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus/pull/1271#discussion_r4321122571)
Review effort: Balanced

The new BF16 MegaMoE forward synchronizes with the host and cannot be CUDA-graph captured. However, `examples/megatron/models/deepseek-v4/run_deepseek_v4.sh:116–126` still recommends full-layer capture with MegaMoE and selects it when `USE_TURBO_MEGA_MOE=True ENABLE_CUDA_GRAPH=True`. This previously supported combination now fails during capture. Reject capture scopes that include MegaMoE, or exclude MegaMoE from capture, and update the launcher guidance as part of adopting this revision.

nodes.body: This Turbo revision requires FlyDSL 0.3.4.1, which removes `flydsl.expr.buffer_ops`. MiniMax-M3 still imports it in `flydsl/index_block_max.py:41`, `msa_token_fwd.py:59`, and `msa_token_bwd.py:65`. Since `primus/configs/models/megatron/minimax_m3.yaml:89` defaults to `msa_backend: flydsl`, the default backend now raises ImportError, even without MegaMoE. The DeepSeek-V4 `flydsl_v1` kernels also retain this import. Port these in-tree kernels to the new FlyDSL API alongside the dependency bump; updating the dependency alone breaks existing training configurations.
